recommendation_before_coding.1_wf_o1_cause: One classification mistake shared by intent but not by code: window spans live in OPENING_SPAN, so the second form (WALL_FACE x H - window rectangles + lintels + heads) loses the wall plane through every window and then also deducts the window rectangle; windows have no below-sill / above-head surfaces at all in V1.
recommendation_before_coding.2_v2_fix: One wall-plane identity: every span on a wall line (wall face, window, door, sliding door, floor-reaching glazing) belongs to the plane; an opening removes exactly its rectangle clipped to [0, H]. METHOD A from the conservation pass: (sum of plane span lengths) x H - sum of rectangles + head faces. METHOD B from explicitly generated surface records: WALL_FACE (full-height spans) + BELOW_SILL (w x sill) + ABOVE_OPENING (w x (H - top)) + HEAD_FACE. Different data paths, predeclared tolerance, any mismatch -> BLOCKED; a separate reconcile() is tested against a deliberately broken surface list; every area test asserts state == COMPUTED.
recommendation_before_coding.3_topology_unchanged: YES: trade layer only; the topology digest must stay the R8.17 digest.
recommendation_before_coding.4_height_as_evidence_object: YES: WALL_HEIGHT_AUTHORITY per (project, revision, floor / measurement scope, trade) with ranked candidates: source finish height > section / elevation clear height > derived from authoritative components > source-bound owner / project fact > permitted project default > BLOCKED. No Urban constant.
recommendation_before_coding.5_315_scope: YES: QORTUBA new revision, the selected region / plan, DRY_INTERNAL_ROOM, trades PLASTER and PAINT only; the 4.00 - 0.60 - 0.15 - 0.10 arithmetic is stored as OWNER_RATIONALE (components not source-established), never a formula.
recommendation_before_coding.6_320_separate: YES: the wet / service tile fact stays its own authority and trade. The owner's own dry rationale implies ~3.15 m usable height, below the 3.20 m tile: recorded as POTENTIAL_PHYSICAL_CONFLICT_NOT_PROVEN (rationale components are not source facts; wet rooms may differ) - never clipped, not asked.
recommendation_before_coding.7_future_derivation: gross vertical height from source levels (finished-floor to finished-floor, or slab to slab with the build-up as a component) MINUS each established deduction (beam / soffit zone where the finish stops at it, ceiling / service / decor zone, floor build-up when the gross is slab-based) - each component carrying its own source and authority; the result carries formula, components, state. Floor-to-floor alone is never a wall height.
recommendation_before_coding.8_blocked_when_a_component_is_unknown: YES at that rank: a derivation with one unknown required component is BLOCKED (never filled with a default); resolution falls to the next rank (an owner / project fact). For Qortuba: only the 4.00 m level exists in source -> derivation BLOCKED -> rank 4 owner fact 3.15 m.
recommendation_before_coding.9_reveal_authority_separation: Physical reveal (geometry + owning side, from frame / leaf / track position) is kept apart from its FINISH state: PLASTER_DEFAULT (owner rule), PLASTER_AND_PAINT (only when the owning side is a painted dry surface), PORCELAIN_EXPLICIT (only with explicit authority), OTHER_EXPLICIT, UNRESOLVED (ownership or surface not established - that reveal only). A wet / service owner never gets paint by default.
recommendation_before_coding.10_profile_position: The frame / track plane splits the wall depth: each side owns the depth between its face and the nearest frame line; a frame flush with a face leaves that side no reveal. A reveal face not drawn on its side (cavity) is UNRESOLVED, never invented.
recommendation_before_coding.11_publish_this_round: YES as SHADOW authorised subtotals per room after the frozen blind V2 run, IF both area methods reconcile everywhere. The COMPLETE plaster / paint / tile rows stay null: column faces (dry and wet) and the duct have no finish authority (R-13 misread in R8.17) - listed as UNRESOLVED contributors with their areas, never silently excluded.
recommendation_before_coding.12_waterproofing: YES, same round, own frozen policy (WATERPROOFING_POLICY_V1): floor membrane = wet-room TS01 floor area; upturn path = the GROSS site boundary (doorway / sliding-door / column / window lines all included; internal obstacle perimeters included); 0.15 m; independent of skirting, wall tile and marble.
13_disagreements_with_chatgpt: R-13 gives no column-face finish authority (R8.17 cited it wrongly): column faces must be UNRESOLVED for plaster, paint AND wet tile until the owner states it - one new owner question.

Two 'independent' area checks are only independent if they read different data (aggregated span lengths vs generated surface records); the 'broken fixture' must be a broken surface list fed to the reconciliation - a correct engine cannot be made to emit one.

Hinged-door reveal ownership is deterministic too (closed-leaf line = frame face), not only the sliding door's: every apartment door reveal faces a dry room -> PLASTER_AND_PAINT, none is 'wet context'.
The glazing line drawn on a window's room face is a plan convention, not frame evidence: window reveals keep the US-07 0.25 m fallback depth.
WET_WALL_TILE_PREP is the same surface set as WALL_TILE (US-03: the tile-prep trade carries the ceramic face) - its own row, never plaster.
The 3.15 m dry rationale conflicts in principle with 3.20 m wet tile: flag, do not clip, do not ask (not proven by source).
